subject: Air-gapped feasibility & staged dedicated fleet for HealthCorp pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@healthcorp.com>, compliance@healthcorp.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Air-gapped feasibility & staged dedicated fleet for HealthCorp pilot

Tom / HealthCorp compliance team — thanks again for the time this morning. As promised, attaching the initial data-use questionnaire and a first-cut proposed fleet layout. High level ask: we need to confirm whether the pilot needs a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment or whether a VPC-private deployment with dedicated GPUs (no multi-tenant co-residency) meets your security checklist.

Quick summary of options we should decide between this week:
- Option A — Private/Air-gapped: physical on-prem appliance, isolated network, HSM-backed keys, no external egress. Longer procurement (~8–12 weeks), requires on-site validation. Better for PHI-heavy workloads that demand no cloud connectivity.
- Option B — Dedicated (VPC) reserved capacity: dedicated GPU pools in HealthCorp's cloud account or Redwood-managed but isolated tenants with strict egress controls and KMS integration. Faster (~2–4 weeks to spin up), supports streaming and automated rollouts, still provides audit logs and per-tenant KV cache control.

Key technical differences to confirm for sizing and runbook:
1) Peak concurrency and p95 latency SLO for the pilot (your number needed).
2) Typical sequence length and longest expected context window (affects memory/KV sizing).
3) Allowed model family / quantization (we can serve same open model variants but air-gap may restrict some optimizations).
4) Expected tokens/day for cost amortization and procurement commit sizing.

Action items for us this week:
- HealthCorp: confirm whether procurement can accept a managed-dedicated VPC or needs an air-gapped appliance.
- Redwood (Aditya/Markus): produce a rapid cost + lead-time comparison for Option A vs Option B, and a minimal test plan for on-site validation.

Attaching: MA-DataUse-Questionnaire-HealthCorp.pdf, proposed-fleet-layout.xlsx

Thanks — Kimberly
--

Subject: Re: Air-gapped feasibility & staged dedicated fleet for HealthCorp pilot

Adding a few technical notes after reviewing their questionnaire draft. Tom — short answers inline, longer notes below.

1) Concurrency: If pilot is <= 200 concurrent requests with p95 latency target <= 250ms, Dedicated VPC (NVIDIA H200 equivalent) with autoscale headroom is likely sufficient. If concurrency spikes beyond 500 consistently, private on-prem with multiple nodes is safer to guarantee tail latency.
2) Context length: 16k tokens vs 32k matters. 32k will increase RAM/KV by ~2.2x for our runtime; this pushes more GPUs or higher memory instances for the private appliance.
3) Quantization: we can quantize to 4-bit for cost in Dedicated mode; air-gapped appliance may restrict third-party kernel updates (so pick a quantization profile we can ship validated).
4) Data residency: VPC-dedicated supports KMS + HSM integration. For absolute 'no egress' requirement, appliance only.

Proposal for an accelerated path (staged):
- Stage 1 (2–4 weeks): Dedicated VPC with reserved capacity for pilot traffic; we implement strict network ACLs, private peering, KMS, and retention/audit configuration. This gets you live fast and validates app behavior.
- Stage 2 (parallel, 8–12 weeks): Provision on-prem appliance for final regulated rollout if procurement mandates air-gap. Use the live pilot telemetry to size exact GPU count and disk/KV persistence needs so the on-prem spec matches real load.

Sizing note (very rough):
- Pilot expected TPS 80, p95 300ms => 4x H100-class workers (or 6x smaller memory GPUs) for Dedicated. If 32k context, bump to ~7 workers. On-prem appliance baseline: 8 x A100/H100 nodes with shared NVMe KV for low-latency cold lookups.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with both cost/lead-time columns and a minimal validation checklist.

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly and Aditya — helpful summary. A few clarifications from the compliance side:

- HealthCorp policy requires 'no external network egress' for any workload that processes unredacted PHI. For the pilot, we can redact PII, but the long-term plan must be air-gapped. Procurement is open to a staged approach so long as the contract includes a commitment to deliver an on-prem appliance within the agreed timeline.
- We need a binding SLA for data deletion and audit log retention (60 months) — please include retention policies in the runbook.
- Can you confirm which telemetry fields Redwood will collect in Stage 1? We need an allowlist.

Next steps: please send a short binding milestone schedule (Stage 1 go-live date, Stage 2 delivery date) and the specific list of telemetry + operator access for Stage 1. We'll use that to brief procurement and legal.

- Tom
Director, Security & Compliance, HealthCorp

Subject: Re: Air-gapped feasibility & staged dedicated fleet for HealthCorp pilot

Tom — great questions. Drafting the milestone schedule and telemetry allowlist below; I'm attaching the proposed-fleet-layout.xlsx with explicit GPU counts and the validation checklist.

Milestone schedule (binding draft):
- Stage 1 (Dedicated VPC): Kickoff 2028-08-15, config & peering 1 week, provision reserved capacity 2 weeks, test window 1 week -> targeted go-live 2028-09-05.
- Stage 2 (On-prem appliance): Hardware order placed 2028-08-20, delivery & install 6–8 weeks (targeted delivery 2028-10-15), on-site validation and HSM key provisioning 2 weeks -> final acceptance 2028-10-29.

Telemetry allowlist (Stage 1):
- Allowed: request latency (ms), success/error codes, token counts per request, ephemeral model selection logs (model id + timestamp), aggregated GPU utilization (no per-request payloads).
- Disallowed: request payloads, generated outputs, full prompt text, or any PII content.

Retention / SLA notes:
- Audit logs: write-once retention policy 60 months; we will provide export to HealthCorp S3 nightly.
- Deletion: PIR-based deletion within 24 hours of a validated deletion request for any metadata that can be purged; raw request payloads are never stored in staged Dedicated if allowlist enforced.

Sizing callouts from the attached spreadsheet:
- Pilot (expected avg TPS 18, peak 80): Dedicated VPC -> 5 x h2-standard (H200-equivalent) instances with continuous batching; buffer capacity for 2x burst.
- On-prem appliance recommendation -> 8 x H100-class nodes, 1 x NVMe node for KV persistence, 2 x management nodes. This gives headroom for model variants and 32k contexts.

I'll convert the milestone to a short PDF for signature and drop the telemetry allowlist into the DocuSign envelope. Kimberly — can you coordinate legal/procurement alignment and confirm whether we need a separate SOC2 addendum for Stage 1?

— Markus
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
